text: Local media report a scandal in the Bulgarian church “Saint George the Victorious” in Edirne; the reason is a request by Greek clerics for a divine service in the Greek language (09.05.2026 15:36)

Local media report a scandal in the Bulgarian church “Saint George the Victorious” in Edirne due to the insistence of Greek clerics to conduct the service for Saint George’s Day in the Greek language.
As a result of this situation, the board of the Constantinople Bulgarians has imposed a ban on divine services in the Bulgarian churches in Adrianople in the Greek language.

According to information from the website “Batı Express”, the scandal broke out when the Greek metropolitan, who was supposed to lead the service in the Bulgarian Orthodox church located in the Edirne neighborhood of Kıyık, insisted that it be conducted in the Greek language. The metropolitan was sent by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in Istanbul.

However, the hundreds of Bulgarians present in the church opposed the Greek cleric. A scandal ensued, as the Bulgarian citizens insisted that in the Bulgarian church, services should be conducted in Bulgarian and not in the Greek language, which they do not understand, the cited source points out.

St. George's Day is also the patronal feast of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church in the Edirne neighborhood of Kıyık, and hundreds of Bulgarians have arrived specifically for the holiday, local media report.
The scandal caused a very strong resonance among the community of Orthodox Bulgarians in Istanbul, and the topic was also covered by other media such as "Habertürk", "Yeni Birlik" and others.

"On behalf of the Istanbul Bulgarian community, we came to Edirne today to conduct the traditional worship service. We are the parish and the owners of this church /including the 'Saints Constantine and Helena' church in Edirne/. Upon our arrival, however, we were informed through priests sent by the Greek Metropolitan of Edirne that we would not be able to conduct worship services in the Bulgarian language. Instead, we were told that the services would be conducted with Greek priests. We did not accept this. Because this is a Bulgarian church and we believe that the services should be conducted in the Bulgarian language," stated the chairman of the board of the Foundation of the Orthodox Churches of the Bulgarian Exarchate in Istanbul and of the community of Constantinople Bulgarians, Dimitri Yotef. "Therefore, as the Foundation of Orthodox Bulgarians, we have made the following decision. From today, we are closing our church for worship services until the issue of conducting services in the Bulgarian language is resolved. At the same time, we decided to ban the Metropolitan of Edirne from entering the church until permission is given for services in the Bulgarian language. Of course, it will be open for visits. People can come and pray, light candles. There is no obstacle to that. However, services will not be held," added Yotef, as quoted by local media. According to him, the decision applies to both churches in the city of Edirne. “To be honest, this decision should have been made years ago. We experienced great sorrow after the death of the late Father Aleksandar Chakaruk. He was very precious to us. Since his death, over the past three years, we have been subjected to strong pressure from the Metropolitan. Therefore, today we met with the board of directors and reached the point of making this decision," he added.

Official Bulgarian representatives were also present in the church for today's service. “Today, a very unpleasant incident occurred in our church, which you all witnessed. We can call it an unexpected situation, but it must also be said that this is a continuation of a long-standing problem. Because we have been facing the same difficulties for a long time. His Holiness the Metropolitan imposed a restriction on conducting services in the Bulgarian language. In the Republic of Turkey, however, services and worship in every church or place of worship are performed in the language of the respective community. The Republic of Turkey is a state that equally protects the rights of different peoples, different denominations, and religious groups. With regret, however, I must state that His Holiness the Metropolitan did not understand our sensitivity on this issue. He may be of Greek origin, but the issue here is the language, the culture, and the right of the community to practice its faith in its own language,” stated the Bulgarian Consul General in Edirne, Radoslava Kafedzhiyska, to the Edirne media.

After quite lengthy and heated disputes, and primarily because of the persistent demands of Bulgarian citizens in defense of their right to offer their prayers in the Bulgarian language, a prayer was read in the Bulgarian language.

The scandals surrounding the Bulgarian churches in Edirne are primarily related to attempts at interference by the Ecumenical Patriarchate, bans on worship in the Bulgarian language, and disputes over the management of the churches. Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew is criticized for actions aimed at imposing a Greek presence, including through services in the Greek language, point out specialists familiar with the issue.

In the Bulgarian churches in Istanbul, "Saint Stephen" and "Saint John of Rila" in the Bulgarian Exarchate, the worship service is conducted in the Bulgarian language, with the only exception being a visit from the Ecumenical Patriarch, when the prayers are offered in Greek.
